input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: The condition uses all(...) where the docstring and title say the section is shown if at least one argument is documented. It should be any(...). With all(), a single undocumented argument suppresses the whole section.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with two arguments where only one has help. all() returns False, so the "Positional arguments" section is omitted and the documented argument disappears from --help. Previously that argument was listed. Also, with no arguments at all, all([]) is True, so an empty "Positional arguments" section header is emitted for every command without arguments.
critique: The finding identifies the same all() vs any() error in the guard. It describes both consequences: a single undocumented argument suppresses the section, and all([]) produces an empty header for commands with no arguments.
